cycle1_result: Females 50–74 (n=13,519) and ≥75 (n=4,883). Bone-sparing agent in those aged 50–74 with fragility fracture and confirmed osteoporosis 47.9% (23/48); in those ≥75 with fragility fracture 39.5% (118/181). Fragility fracture recorded 8.8% (15/171) aged 50–74 and 0.8% (65/8110) aged ≥75.
intervention: Introduction of a community-based fracture liaison nurse who reviewed the practice population meeting the inclusion criteria.

title: "Early Trigger" Intravenous Vitamin K: Optimizing Target-Driven Care in Warfarinised Patients With Hip Fracture.

cycle1_result: Warfarinised patients on oral vitamin K protocol: mean time to theatre 53.71 hours; 79% breached BPT due to anticoagulation.

change: Trauma Meeting/Post-Take Ward Round proforma on yellow paper, designed with the team (PDSA cycles), results presented at departmental teaching, and weekend surgical juniors briefed to attend the trauma meeting and complete it.

cycle1_result: 72% seen on PTWR, 47% of these clearly labelled; 64% of those not seen were weekend admissions; no consultant on take identifiable in 19%, presenting complaint missing in 78%, no plan in 3%, not timed in 17%, no name 19%, no signature 14%, no grade 50%, no contact details 25%.

title: Revolutionising rapid recovery: a quality improvement project in hip and knee replacement.
standard: Local SMART aim: 90% of cases mobilising on day 0 and length of stay reduced by 1 day within 1 year, with increased throughput
finding: Mean length of stay 3.6 days for both total hip and total knee replacement; Model Hospital median length of stay 4.2 days (hips, 41st nationally) and 3.9 days (knees, 34th).
change: Multidisciplinary Rapid Recovery Group with parallel PDSA cycles: ropivacaine local infiltration protocol, oxycodone MR, preprinted drug charts, Taurus frames and nurse-led mobilisation, stopping routine MSU and TED stockings, and a ring-fenced elective ward.
setting: North Devon District Hospital, elective hip and knee replacement pathway
cycle1_result: Mean length of stay 3.6 days for both total hip and total knee replacement; Model Hospital median length of stay 4.2 days (hips, 41st nationally) and 3.9 days (knees, 34th).
intervention: Multidisciplinary Rapid Recovery Group with parallel PDSA cycles: ropivacaine local infiltration protocol, oxycodone MR, preprinted drug charts, Taurus frames and nurse-led mobilisation, stopping routine MSU and TED stockings, and a ring-fenced elective ward.
cycle2_result: Mean length of stay fell to 2.4 days for hips and 2.0 days for knees (p<0.0001); all patients mobilised on day 0 in the most recent 3 months; predicted yearly throughput 560 vs 480.

setting: Spine Unit, Orthopaedic and Trauma Surgery Department, Assiut University Hospitals (tertiary spine centre)
cycle1_result: All patients received a correct preoperative first-generation cephalosporin dose, but IV antibiotics continued 1–6 days followed by oral antibiotics until suture removal (up to two weeks) in all patients, with mixed agents; SSI 1 case (1.85%).
intervention: New local surgical antibiotic prophylaxis protocol (first-generation cephalosporin 30–60 minutes before incision, redose after 3 hours, stop at 24 hours) agreed in discussion sessions and disseminated by pamphlet and theatre poster.
cycle2_result: All patients received preoperative first-generation cephalosporin continued for only 24 hours postoperatively and were discharged on day 2; no SSI.
other_findings: Difference in infection rates was not statistically significant; mean postoperative stay fell from 3.33 to 2.04 days.

topic: Fracture clinic standards and virtual fracture clinic
title: Optimizing orthopedic trauma care delivery during the COVID-19 pandemic. A closed-loop audit of implementing a virtual fracture clinic and fast-track pathway in a Dutch level 2 trauma center.
standard: Predefined standards from national coronavirus outpatient guidelines and local consensus: (1) all eligible ED trauma patients referred for VFC review; (2) all patients contacted after VFC review; (3) patient-initiated follow-up by default where possible; (4) follow-up by telephone or video where possible. Target 100% for standard 1.
finding: 162/184 (88.0%) referred for VFC review; 98.1% reached afterwards (3 patients, 1.9%, not reached); 29/162 (17.9%) discharged 'virtually'; 137/291 (45.0%) appointments remote. Median total ED time 95 minutes vs 131 minutes at baseline (p<0.001).
change: After an evaluation meeting, ED staff were invited to attend VFC review for direct feedback, presentations explaining the workflow were held, posters were put up in the ED, and a patient information leaflet asking patients to call if not contacted by 15:00 the next workday was introduced.
setting: OLVG, a level 2 trauma centre and teaching hospital in Amsterdam (emergency department and virtual fracture clinic)
cycle1_result: 162/184 (88.0%) referred for VFC review; 98.1% reached afterwards (3 patients, 1.9%, not reached); 29/162 (17.9%) discharged 'virtually'; 137/291 (45.0%) appointments remote. Median total ED time 95 minutes vs 131 minutes at baseline (p<0.001).
intervention: After an evaluation meeting, ED staff were invited to attend VFC review for direct feedback, presentations explaining the workflow were held, posters were put up in the ED, and a patient information leaflet asking patients to call if not contacted by 15:00 the next workday was introduced.
cycle2_result: 302/305 (98.4%) referred for VFC review; 99.0% reached afterwards (3 patients, 1.0%, not reached); 41/302 (13.6%) discharged 'virtually'; 179/436 (41.1%) appointments remote. Median total ED time 98 minutes (−33 minutes vs baseline, p=0.001); time to review 47 minutes (p<0.001); time for review 35 minutes vs 45 minutes (p=0.019).
other_findings: An ED orthopaedic trauma fast-track pathway was introduced alongside the VFC; 88% and 92% of suspected fracture patients were treated in fast-track rooms. Median VFC review time was 9 minutes then 7 minutes per patient.
authors: Geerdink TH; Salentijn DA; de Vries KA; Noordman PCW; van Dongen JM; Haverlag R; Goslings JC; van Veen RN

title: Introduction of an enhanced recovery programme for total shoulder arthroplasty: report of a novel pathway.
standard: not reported
finding: Pre-enhanced recovery: mean LOS 2.38 nights, median 2 nights, single night stay rate 40.2%; complication rate 9.9%.
change: Enhanced recovery programme via PDSA cycles: MDT-led preoperative class with OT home assessment, new patient information booklet and DVD, standardised anaesthetic/analgesic protocol with carbohydrate and gabapentin loading, and a physiotherapy protocol with sling for comfort only and early safe-zone mobilisation.
setting: Derby Shoulder Unit, University Hospitals of Derby and Burton NHS Foundation Trust
cycle1_result: Pre-enhanced recovery: mean LOS 2.38 nights, median 2 nights, single night stay rate 40.2%; complication rate 9.9%.

cycle1_result: 13.9% (n=11) assessed for bone protection; 1.3% (n=1) prescribed a bisphosphonate and 10.1% (n=8) other bone protection; 86.1% (n=68) neither assessed nor prescribed.

topic: Elective cancellations due to asymptomatic bacteriuria
title: Introduction of a New Protocol to Limit the Number of Cancelled Elective Orthopaedic Operations Due to Asymptomatic Bacteriuria.
standard: not reported
finding: Of 33 all-cause cancellations, 7 (21.2%) were cancelled for UTI risk on positive urinalysis; only 1 (14.3%) of these was symptomatic, so 6 (85.7%) were cancelled for asymptomatic bacteriuria.
change: New symptom-based protocol from 1 May 2019: all patients complete a 7-item UTI symptom questionnaire and surgery is cancelled only if two or more symptoms are reported, regardless of urinalysis.
setting: Lister Hospital, Stevenage (East & North Herts NHS Trust), large district general hospital offering tertiary orthopaedic services; cancelled elective orthopaedic operations
cycle1_result: Of 33 all-cause cancellations, 7 (21.2%) were cancelled for UTI risk on positive urinalysis; only 1 (14.3%) of these was symptomatic, so 6 (85.7%) were cancelled for asymptomatic bacteriuria.
intervention: New symptom-based protocol from 1 May 2019: all patients complete a 7-item UTI symptom questionnaire and surgery is cancelled only if two or more symptoms are reported, regardless of urinalysis.
cycle2_result: Of 45 all-cause cancellations, 2 (4.4%) were cancelled for UTI risk, both symptomatic; 4 (8.8%) had positive urinalysis, the 2 asymptomatic ones cancelled for unrelated reasons. No cancellations for asymptomatic bacteriuria; estimated 71.4% reduction in cancellations for UTI risk.
other_findings: Patients with positive urinalysis whose operations were not cancelled were not captured, so the true effect is estimated. Each cancelled operation was estimated to waste 2.1 hours of theatre time (about £2,525).

finding: Skin status documented 37%; isolation method documented 43%; tourniquet pressure documented 71%; pressure within BOAST safe limit 25%; tourniquet time under 120 minutes in 97%.

cycle1_result: Skin status documented 37%; isolation method documented 43%; tourniquet pressure documented 71%; pressure within BOAST safe limit 25%; tourniquet time under 120 minutes in 97%.
intervention: Results presented at departmental audit meeting; tourniquet details made a mandatory part of the electronic operation note template; labels on tourniquet machines to calculate pressure; BOAST guidance posted in the theatre doctors' office.

finding: Exsanguination method documented 5.6%, isolation (shut-off drape) 2.4%, skin condition 0%; duration not in operative note 23.0%, not recorded at all 1.6%; > 120 min in 1.6%; pressure within standard in 24.3% lower limb, 34.8% upper limb and 66.7% paediatric cases.
change: Local presentation at trust Quality & Safety Half Day and 'PRESSURE' mnemonic posters in theatres and offices, followed by a new electronic patient record with a tourniquet section and BOAST-based auto-text proforma in the operation note.
setting: Ashford and St Peter's Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust; trauma and elective orthopaedic surgery across both sites
cycle1_result: Exsanguination method documented 5.6%, isolation (shut-off drape) 2.4%, skin condition 0%; duration not in operative note 23.0%, not recorded at all 1.6%; > 120 min in 1.6%; pressure within standard in 24.3% lower limb, 34.8% upper limb and 66.7% paediatric cases.
intervention: Local presentation at trust Quality & Safety Half Day and 'PRESSURE' mnemonic posters in theatres and offices, followed by a new electronic patient record with a tourniquet section and BOAST-based auto-text proforma in the operation note.

cycle1_result: Mean time to reduction 532 minutes (240–804); 4 (29%) reduced within 6 hours and 11 (79%) within 12 hours (abstract gives 28.6% and 71.4%). ED reductions (n=2) mean 275 minutes vs theatre (n=13) 576 minutes.

setting: Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother Hospital, Margate, Kent; main orthopaedic ward and outlier wards
cycle1_result: 93% (106/113) seen by a physiotherapist on the day of or day after surgery (main orthopaedic ward 94%, 80/85; outliers 93%, 21/28; P=0.3). 40% (46/113) had delayed mobilisation. 83% (94/113) had two hours of physiotherapy in the first week. cycle1_result: Mean time from referral to image transfer 18 hours; 36% (n=14) transferred within 1 hour; neurosurgery response averaged 18 hours with 38% (n=14) reviewed within 6 hours.

topic: Suspected cauda equina time to MRI
title: Improving the suspected cauda equina syndrome pathway at a district general hospital: a quality improvement project.
standard: GIRFT National Suspected CES Pathway 2023: emergency MRI within 4 hours of request; local SMART aim of median under 4 hours from ED attendance to MRI within 1 year
finding: Median time from ED presentation to MRI 5.9 hours (IQR 4.9–14.7) although median MRI request to scan was 1.7 hours (IQR 1.1–3.7), meeting the GIRFT target; 8% of patients incorrectly sent to the GP-led MEDOCC service. At PDSA 1: 38% of MRIs unnecessary, 0.5 CES MRIs/day, time to analgesia 5.3 hours (IQR 3.8–7.0), 9% inappropriately triaged to MEDOCC.
change: Three PDSA cycles (July 2023 to January 2024): CES working group and trust-level awareness; new locally adapted SOP based on the GIRFT pathway with CES-specific shorter MRI sequences; ED triage and assessment posters, board round, grand round and senior-led teaching. Planned extension of MRI hours was not achieved.
setting: Medway Maritime Hospital, Gillingham; district general hospital emergency department without on-site emergency spinal surgery
cycle1_result: Median time from ED presentation to MRI 5.9 hours (IQR 4.9–14.7) although median MRI request to scan was 1.7 hours (IQR 1.1–3.7), meeting the GIRFT target; 8% of patients incorrectly sent to the GP-led MEDOCC service. At PDSA 1: 38% of MRIs unnecessary, 0.5 CES MRIs/day, time to analgesia 5.3 hours (IQR 3.8–7.0), 9% inappropriately triaged to MEDOCC.
intervention: Three PDSA cycles (July 2023 to January 2024): CES working group and trust-level awareness; new locally adapted SOP based on the GIRFT pathway with CES-specific shorter MRI sequences; ED triage and assessment posters, board round, grand round and senior-led teaching. Planned extension of MRI hours was not achieved.
cycle2_period: PDSA 3, cycles run July 2023 to January 2024
cycle2_result: Approximately 27 patients per cycle. Median ED presentation to MRI 5.7 hours (IQR 4.1–14.3), primary aim not met; GIRFT 4-hour request-to-scan target met in all cycles. other_findings: Time to MRI rose to 9.9 hours in PDSA 2 amid ED pressures and industrial action; 43/81 patients presented at times making same-day MRI unlikely because scanners ran only until 20:00, and by PDSA 3 attendance to MRI request was still a median 3.9 hours.

intervention: Nurse-led multidisciplinary team with nutrition support nurses; daily 20-minute staff training over five days; updated NRS2002 form in the nursing IT system with fixed screening time points and automated reminders; 24-hour dietary energy and protein record sheet; dietary lists, leaflets, education manuals, QR codes, videos and teach-back; ward ONS supply protocol; discharge follow-up manual and smart cloud follow-up platform.

change: Enhanced Recovery Canada recommendations: pre-emptive nausea prophylaxis (aprepitant, scopolamine patch), pre-emptive multimodal oral analgesia, and lidocaine epidural anaesthesia via a 'STAR Module' in the electronic order set, supported by STAR rounds, website posts and a video; then a switch to spinal lidocaine.

cycle1_result: Standard cohort: 57/105 (54.3%) discharged same day; complications preventing same-day discharge 48 (45.7%); unscheduled 30-day hospital encounters 11 (10.5%).

standard: NELA guidelines for risk assessment and documentation in emergency laparotomy

title: EGS P33 Audit of Serial Lactate Measurement in Septic Patients Admitted in Acute General Surgery Department
standard: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021: lactate measured within 3 hours of admission and repeated within 4–6 hours if ≥2 mmol
finding: Surgical ward: lactate repeated in 16 (28.6%) patients with high lactate, 9 (56%) of these at ≥8 hours. HDU/ICU: 12 (92%) had lactate repeated in the target time.
setting: Acute general surgery department, University Hospital Hairmyres, East Kilbride; single centre retrospective audit
cycle1_result: Surgical ward: lactate repeated in 16 (28.6%) patients with high lactate, 9 (56%) of these at ≥8 hours. HDU/ICU: 12 (92%) had lactate repeated in the target time.
intervention: not reported
other_findings: Standards were not achieved on the ward, attributed to unawareness of recommendations and time pressure.
authors: Hobeita W; Ali K; Khan K
citation: Hobeita W, Ali K, Khan K. EGS P33 Audit of Serial Lactate Measurement in Septic Patients Admitted in Acute General Surgery Department. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad348.079.

title: EGS P34 CEPOD Booking Audit in General Surgery

title: OGC P09 Benchmarking of OG cancer care across the United Kingdom: a collaboration of 2 national clinical audit systems
standard: not reported
finding: Staging CT: England 83.1%, Scotland 98.5%, Wales 92.2%. MDT curative treatment plans: England 40%, Scotland 29%, Wales 34%; actual curative treatment 24–31%. Longitudinal margin positivity: Scotland 2.4%, England 5.4%, Wales 8.2%.
setting: National clinical audits: NOGCA (England and Wales) and Scottish QPI data
cycle1_result: Staging CT: England 83.1%, Scotland 98.5%, Wales 92.2%. MDT curative treatment plans: England 40%, Scotland 29%, Wales 34%; actual curative treatment 24–31%. Longitudinal margin positivity: Scotland 2.4%, England 5.4%, Wales 8.2%.
intervention: not reported

title: OGC P35 A clinical audit looking at how efficient the current pathways are for detecting upper oesophageal cancer
standard: NHS England 62-day referral to treatment standard; NICE: urgent OGD for dysphagia and barium swallow not first line
finding: Of 348 oesophageal cancers, 14 cervical cases; 9 analysed. 6/9 first referred to ENT. 4/9 had OGD, 5/9 barium swallow (4/5 as first-line) and 7/9 rigid oesophagoscopy. Median GP referral to treatment 108 days vs 62-day standard.
setting: Head and neck and upper GI cancer pathways, Belfast City Hospital
cycle1_result: Of 348 oesophageal cancers, 14 cervical cases; 9 analysed. 6/9 first referred to ENT. 4/9 had OGD, 5/9 barium swallow (4/5 as first-line) and 7/9 rigid oesophagoscopy. Median GP referral to treatment 108 days vs 62-day standard.
intervention: not reported
other_findings: Authors recommend direct visualisation of the oesophagus for red flag dysphagia regardless of whether assessed by head and neck or upper GI pathway.
authors: Siempis T; Harris A; McCain S; Kennedy R; MacAulay G; Gray R; Kennedy A
citation: Siempis T, Harris A, McCain S, Kennedy R, MacAulay G, Gray R, et al.. OGC P35 A clinical audit looking at how efficient the current pathways are for detecting upper oesophageal cancer. British Journal of Surgery. 2023;110(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znad348.233.

topic: Postoperative pneumonia diagnosis and antibiotic choice
title: OGC P61 Audit of diagnosis and treatment of early pneumonia after elective oesophagogastric resections
standard: US CDC criteria for pneumonia diagnosis and NICE guidelines for antibiotic choice
finding: 30.2% treated with antibiotics for pneumonia; 42.4% of these had sputum taken at suspicion; 69.7% prescribed a NICE-approved antibiotic; 17.4% met CDC pneumonia criteria.

cycle1_result: 30.2% treated with antibiotics for pneumonia; 42.4% of these had sputum taken at suspicion; 69.7% prescribed a NICE-approved antibiotic; 17.4% met CDC pneumonia criteria.

standard: NICE: PET-CT for all oesophageal and OGJ cancers except T1a

cycle1_result: Mean wait for PET-CT 17 (1–57) days; 14 (32%) had CT/PET-CT discrepancy; 5 (11%) distant metastasis on PET-CT; 9 (20%) incidental uptake; further investigations added mean 15 (1–28) days delay.

standard: NELA frailty and care of the elderly review recommendations (compared with 31.8% in 8th NELA report)

cycle1_result: 98.6% had documented Clinical Frailty Scale score (mean 3.6); 87.7% reviewed by SAFT; 63.3% had pre-operative frailty review.
intervention: Frailty screening on admission, weekly ELLSA MDT and designated ELLSA MDT board introduced, aiming for 100% geriatrician review.
other_findings: 70% discharged home independently; 7% needed a care package.

finding: Baseline cardio-metabolic assessment in 50–65%; less than 15% at 3–6 months. Body weight and blood pressure documented at 3–6 months in 15% and 2.5% respectively. Collaboration with GP for annual health check 78–100%.
setting: Intellectual Disability community psychiatry service
cycle1_result: Baseline cardio-metabolic assessment in 50–65%; less than 15% at 3–6 months. Body weight and blood pressure documented at 3–6 months in 15% and 2.5% respectively. Collaboration with GP for annual health check 78–100%.
intervention: not reported
other_findings: Compliance was significantly better when the nursing team was involved. Re-audit planned in one year after action plan dissemination (community nurse involvement, sphygmomanometers in every clinic).
authors: Kyaw S; Bintizahari F; Speight P
citation: Kyaw S, Bintizahari F, Speight P. Clinical audit of cardio-metabolic monitoring in people with intellectual disability (PWID) taking antipsychotic medication. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S87-S88. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.268.

cycle1_result: 273 clozapine levels taken; mean interval between levels 10 months 2 weeks (range 2 days to 13 years); 88 levels >600 ug/L and 108 levels <350 ug/L; 32% of levels above recommended range; non-significant positive dose-level trend (R = 0.37)

cycle1_result: Smoking status asked in 68%; not asked n = 11 (32%); smoker not given advice n = 13 (38%); smoker given advice n = 4 (12%); advice or NRT given to only 14% of potential smokers.

cycle1_result: 30% of essential standards not met and 21% somewhat met; 36% of expected standards met, 41% not met; 89% of desirable standards not met.

cycle1_period: Admissions in 2018, reviewed January to May 2019

standard: Standards in the New Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry for components of the psychiatric history
finding: Only patient ID and presenting complaint in 100%; medical history 72%; forensic history 44%; social history 39%.

cycle1_result: 3/33 (9.1%) on antipsychotics >3 months had AIMS; 14 (28.0%) given verbal EPSE information; 12 (24.0%) given information on wider side effects; 19 (38.0%) had documented side-effect assessment at review.

title: Re-audit of use of seclusion in a tier 4 adolescent psychiatric intensive care unit
standard: Trust guidelines on seclusion monitoring and documentation, including consultant review within 24 hours and care plan modification
finding: Average seclusion 30 h; assault on staff as indication in 50%; consultant review within 24 h documented in under 70%; care plan modified in 63%.
change: Daily nursing safety huddles, weekly Incidence Reduction meetings and an ongoing QI project on restrictive practice.
setting: Tier 4 adolescent psychiatric intensive care unit, London
cycle1_result: Average seclusion 30 h; assault on staff as indication in 50%; consultant review within 24 h documented in under 70%; care plan modified in 63%.

cycle2_result: 18 patients, 46 incidents: average seclusion 20 h; consultant review within 24 h over 90%; care plan modification over 95%; just under half of seclusions monitored and documented per Trust guidelines.
